messages.subject: geom_segment and plot resolution
parts:
Hello, 

I would like to plot a tree with lines connecting branches from different clades.

I can do this with geom_segment, but the resolution of the lines seems poor when compared to geom_taxalink.

Is there a way to improve the resolution of lines in geom_segment or more intelligent way of drawing lines between branches?

I have attached example code and pdfs of plots

Cheers
Ollie

library(ggtree)
library(ggplot2)

set.seed(123)
tree <- rtree(30)

# nodes to connect
n1 <- MRCA(tree, tip = c("t18", "t13"))
n2 <- MRCA(tree, tip = c("t2", "t4"))
n3 <- MRCA(tree, tip = c("t29", "t16"))

# create ggtree object
p <- ggtree(tree, branch.length = "none")

# get node info from ggtree object
N1 <- p$data[n1,]
N2 <- p$data[n2,]
N3 <- p$data[n3,]

# plot tree with lines connecting branches
pdf(file = "test-segment.pdf", height = 5, width = 7) 
p + 
  geom_tiplab() +
  geom_segment2(aes(x = N1$x-0.6, xend = N2$x-0.6, y = N1$y, yend = N2$y), colour = "red", size = 0.2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), ends = "both")) +
  geom_segment2(aes(x = N1$x-0.4, xend = N3$x-0.4, y = N1$y, yend = N3$y), colour = "red", size = 0.2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), ends = "both"))
dev.off()


# plot tree with geom_taxalink for comparison
pdf(file = "test-taxalink.pdf", height = 5, width = 7) 
p + 
  geom_tiplab() + 
  geom_taxalink(n1, n2, colour = "red", curvature = 0.2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), ends = "both")) +
  geom_taxalink(n1, n3, colour = "red", curvature = 0.2, arrow = arrow(length = unit(1.5, "mm"), ends = "both"))
dev.off()
